syllabus.scope_note: The written final covers all nine lectures.

style.source: Midterms 1 and 2 and the final practice exam on the course page
question_types: Multiple choice on definitions, categories and rulings
Classify a case (which category, which right, which riba)
"Which is NOT one of..." list questions
Ruling with its reason (why prohibited, why permissible)
Compare two contracts (commercial vs collaborative insurance, bonds vs shares, lease vs installment sale)

chapters.title: Lecture 1 · Concept and characteristics of contemporary financial transactions
Lecture 2 · Ijtihad method and types of rights
Lecture 3 · Incorporeal rights: copyright, patents, trade names
Lecture 5 · Securities and the stock market
Lecture 9 · Sale, installment sale and Murabaha

items.name: Contemporary financial transactions: the term and its definition
items.memorize: Financial cases that emerged in the modern age, changed by progress or circumstances, bear new names, or combine old forms

items.name: Four categories of transactions
items.memorize: Bargains (sale, leasing) · donations (grants, will, waqf) · dropping/isqat (ending a debt) · documentation/tawthiq (mortgage, bail, draft)

items.name: Four kinds of contemporary cases (with examples)
items.memorize: Unknown before (companies, banknotes) · rules updated by progress (key delivery → property registry) · new names for old rulings (bank interest = riba) · combined old forms (murabaha, leasing)

items.name: Relevant terms jurists used
items.memorize: Emerged cases (nawazil), occurrences, incidences (waqi'at), fatwa

items.name: Four characteristics of transactions jurisprudence
items.memorize: Based on general principles · the original ruling is permissibility · based on reasons and benefits · both flexible and constant

items.name: Original ruling: transactions permissible, worship restricted
items.memorize: Worship needs a text to be allowed; transactions are allowed unless a clear text forbids them

items.name: Key texts cited in Lecture 1
items.memorize: An-Nisa 4:29 (no unjust consumption of wealth, mutual consent) · Al-Baqarah 2:275 (trade permitted, riba forbidden) · prohibition of gharar sale · "Muslims keep to their conditions..."

items.name: Five necessities (maqasid) Islam preserves
items.memorize: Faith, life, intellect, lineage, wealth

items.name: What is constant vs flexible in transactions
items.memorize: Constant: consent, no injustice, preserving wealth · flexible: methods, e.g. money from gold and silver to paper

items.name: Nine qualifications of the researcher (mujtahid)
items.memorize: Quran · Sunnah · ijma' · Arabic · talent for ijtihad · honesty (avoid major sins) · maqasid al-shari'ah · deriving rules from scholars' books · understanding the lived reality

items.name: Eight steps to rule on a new case
items.memorize: Pray · understand the case · search Quran and Sunnah · Companions · four imams · recent scholars · own opinion · otherwise refrain from fatwa

items.name: Definition of a right (haqq)
items.memorize: An exclusive entitlement by which the Shari'ah establishes an authority or an obligation

items.name: Classification of rights
items.memorize: Political (election, nomination) · civil → general (body, home) and private → family (custody, divorce) and financial → personal (creditor–debtor), material (property), incorporeal (innovation)

items.name: Classify a given right (political, general, family, personal, material, incorporeal)
Property (mal) and why incorporeal rights count as property
items.memorize: Anything with recognized value among people that may lawfully be used

items.name: Copyright: who is the author, literary vs financial right
items.memorize: Berne Convention 1886 · literary right: permanent, not transferable · financial right: temporary, inheritable · mere collecting without creativity is not protected

items.name: Four reasons intellectual property is legitimate
items.memorize: Benefits are compensable · custom ('urf) recognizes it · plagiarism is prohibited · rights correspond to responsibilities ("the benefit runs with the burden"). Patent omits 'urf

items.name: Patent (1791): inventor's rights and four certificate types
items.memorize: Rights: use it for a limited time, carry the inventor's name · certificates: full-rights, limited, additive (improvements), importation (F.L.A.I.)

items.name: Trade name (1909): trademark, shop sign, location; trademark functions; rights
items.memorize: Components: mark, sign, location (M.S.L.) · trademark functions: distinctiveness, attraction, surveillance · rights: exclusive use, transferable asset · lawful unless based on cheating or gharar

items.name: Insurance: meaning, definition and philosophy
items.memorize: A contractual system of compensation or donation; at heart, collective risk-sharing

items.name: Collaborative insurance: textual root and forms in Islam
items.memorize: Al-Ma'idah 5:2 "cooperate in righteousness" · people of zakat · kinship ('aqilah, blood money) · social solidarity (the Ash'arites)

items.name: Three collaborative insurance systems
items.memorize: Retirement (no gharar: a donation, workers are insurer and insured) · social security · reciprocal (mutual funds). All lawful

items.name: Commercial insurance: elements of the contract and five conditions of the risk
items.memorize: Elements: insurer, insured, risk, installment, insurance amount · risk: uncertain, not intentional, not prohibited, future, regular

items.name: Types of commercial insurance
items.memorize: People (life, casualty) · property · liability

items.name: Why commercial insurance is prohibited, and its three exceptions
items.memorize: Excessive gharar · gambling · both ribas (more back = fadl, same back = nasi'ah) · exceptions: dependent not original (ticket, car rental), necessity, free

items.name: Commercial vs collaborative insurance
items.memorize: Prohibited vs encouraged · compensation vs donation contract · profit vs solidarity · no surplus back vs surplus to participants · personal vs communal

items.name: Securities: title deeds (shares) vs debt deeds (bonds)
Origin of the bourse (Bruges, 1285) and the stock exchange
items.memorize: Brokers trade for clients, dealers for themselves · instruments: stocks, bonds, commodities, foreign exchange

items.name: Regular market vs stock market (four differences)
items.memorize: Face to face vs brokers · goods present vs elsewhere · inspect before buying vs not · real sales vs speculation on prices

items.name: Characteristics and four values of a share
items.memorize: Equal value, indivisible, tradable, nominal value · values: nominal (par), issue (IPO), real (assets − liabilities), market (supply and demand)

items.name: Eight rights of ordinary shareholders
items.memorize: Stay in the company · vote · dividends · dispose of shares · monitor the business · sue the board · priority in new shares · recoup from assets on liquidation

items.name: Preferred and enjoyment shares and why both are prohibited
items.memorize: Preferred: fixed profit regardless (riba) and unequal treatment · enjoyment: redeemed early by lottery, then profit isn't earned (unjust, gharar)

items.name: Capital vs enjoyment shares; in-kind vs cash shares
Conditions for dealing in shares, trading rules and zakat
items.memorize: Halal activity · no riba · known, transparent company · not preferred · not enjoyment · no riba loans, no short selling, installments allowed · zakat: investor (company pays) vs trader (market value at year end)

items.name: Bonds: characteristics and names
items.memorize: Equal value, nominal value, transferable, indivisible · investment certificates (increasing, current yield, lottery prizes), treasury bills (~3 months), loan bonds

items.name: Ordinary vs premium-redeemable vs guaranteed bonds
items.memorize: Premium example: nominal 1000 SAR, paid 900 SAR, the 100 SAR comes back at maturity; interest on the nominal value

items.name: Bonds vs shares (four differences)
items.memorize: Debt vs capital · fixed return vs profit-dependent · no vote vs vote · priority at dissolution vs after debts

items.name: Bonds are prohibited (riba) and the lawful alternatives
items.memorize: Companies: issue shares or partnerships · government: good loans, advancing zakat, voluntary donations, exceptional taxes

items.name: Leasing (ijarah): definition, evidence, lessor vs lessee duties
items.memorize: Lessor: deliver usable asset, bear defects and structural repairs, reclaim at the end · lessee: pay rent, maintain, return the asset

items.name: Lease ending with ownership vs installment sale vs standard lease
items.memorize: Installment sale: one contract, ownership now · lease to own: two contracts (lease, then transfer) · standard lease: one contract, never owns

items.name: Why lease-to-own is not allowed, and the conditions that make it permissible
items.memorize: Rent above market, unclear sale vs lease, unfair loss on default · allowed if: fixed period, fixed installments with no late increase, transfer by gift or nominal sale, no down payment

items.name: Seven conditions of a sale contract
items.memorize: Mutual consent, legal capacity, lawful item, ownership, deliverability, knowledge of goods and price, immediate execution

items.name: Direct installment sale (markup for deferral)
items.memorize: Permissible if the price is fixed (e.g. 50,000 cash vs 60,000 over a year)

items.name: Murabaha: the promise and two contracts, and its conditions
items.memorize: Promise (not binding before the bank buys) → bank buys and owns the item → profit sale to the client · conditions: price fixed, interest inside the price, no extra for late payment, not a ribawi item (gold, dates), guarantee or mortgage allowed
